summary.text: This briefing evaluates the combination of direct preference optimization, instruction following, and safety alignment to balance multi-turn safety, minimize over-refusal, and preserve core capabilities. Evidence shows that internal conflicts between safety alignment and instruction following can cause chaotic trajectories, which direct preference optimization and structured data curation aim to resolve. The DVF assessment yields a Demand score of 1.0, a Feasibility score of 4.0, and a Viability score of null due to missing evidence.

target_user.text: The target user is derived from open-source repository maintainers, benchmark developers, and package users who deploy mixture-of-experts language models and alignment pipelines such as repo:amd-agi/instella-moe, repo:allenai/reward-bench, and pkg:turbo-alignment.

jtbd.text: Balance multi-turn safety alignment, low over-refusal on benign boundary queries, and instruction following under verifiable constraints.

value_prop.text: Align language models using direct preference optimization alongside structured data curation to balance safety and instruction-following objectives without degrading core capabilities.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is axis V (viability), which was explicitly designated due to missing evidence in the bundle. We assume that enterprise customers will pay for a specialized direct preference optimization toolkit that resolves internal safety-instruction conflicts.

mvp.text: Conduct customer interviews and a price acceptance test with proposed threshold 20 potential enterprise buyers to validate willingness to pay for a specialized alignment pipeline.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold: 40 percent positive response rate in willingness-to-pay and pricing acceptance interviews.

kill_criteria.text: Fewer than proposed threshold: 10 percent of interviewed enterprise customers express willingness to pay for the alignment solution.
